Metal-Free Intramolecular Aminophosphination of Allenes
Zhantao Yang, Zhenzhen Sun, Ningning Zhu, Wenyan Li, Meng Han, Yan Qiao, Chun-Hua Yang, *
and Junbiao Chang *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2020, 85, 15686 −15692 Read Online

ABSTRACT: A metal-free intramolecular aminophosphination of sulfonamidoal-
lenes with diarylphosphine oxides and Tf 2O was developed. This method o ﬀers a
general and practical procedure to construct valuable alkenylphosphine-substituted
N-heterocycles via the bifunctionalization reaction of allenes in good yields under
mild conditions.
O
rganophosphorus compounds have drawn tremendous
attention due to the widespread applications as building
blocks of biological molecular, 1 drug and drug candidates, 2 and
ligands3 in organic synthesis. In particular, β-aminophosphines,
bearing unique properties in the ﬁeld of coordination
chemistry and asymmetric catalysis because of their broad
electronic and steric tenability, have gained considerable
attention.4 Furthermore, β-aminophosphines are privileged
structures in drug development, for example, antimalarial, 5
antiviral,6 and antibacterial 7 activities. To this end, signi ﬁcant
eﬀorts have been made toward the preparation of β-
aminophosphines or β-aminophosphonates. The construction
of C −P bonds via the C −C multiple bond bifunctionalization
reaction catalyzed by a transition metal was one of the most
eﬃcient methods. However, this method is usually not feasible
because the transition metal catalyst forms the coordinatively
saturated complex with PR 2Ho rP R 2R′, and the catalytic
activity is reduced or completely lost. 8 Therefore, examples
that are involved in the construction of C −P bonds via C −C
multiple bond bifunctionalization reactions are still limited.
The Yang group reported an e ﬃcient method for the synthesis
of various phosphorated indoles by the cyclization of Ts-
protected o-alkenylanilines catalyzed by Cu (II) in high yield
(Scheme 1 a).
9 Then, they reported a method to synthesize β-
aminophosphonates with oxime phosphonates ( Scheme 1b).10
Zhang et al. discovered a novel intermolecular amino-
phosphinoylation using AgNO 3 to produce a phosphinoyl
radical from diarylphosphine oxides, followed by amination
with CuBr 2 as a catalyst to obtain β-aminophosphonates
(Scheme 1 c).11 Fang et al. also reported a new alkene
bifunctionalization reaction to gain β-aminophosphonates with
anilines and H-phosphonates using FeCl 3 through a radical
process (Scheme 1c).12 Tang and co-workers developed a new

oxidants are usually needed. These requirements have limited
the substrate scope and the practical utility. Therefore, it is still

desirable and essential to develop environmentally benign and
metal-free methods for the direct preparation of β-amino-
phosphine derivatives.
Recently, metal-free C −heteroatom bonding as an environ-
mentally friendly process has garnered interest from the
synthetic community.
14 These methods are very bene ﬁcial as
promising substitutes and valuable supplements for transition-
metal catalytic processes. In 2017, Hirano and Miura et al.
reported a metal-free electrophilic phosphine cyclization of
alkynes.
15 In the presence of Tf 2O/2,6-lutidine, the electro-
philic phosphination reagents, which are produced in situ by
diarylphosphonate oxides, ar e successfully coupled with
alkynes to give 2-phenyl-substituted β-aminophosphination
products ( Scheme 1 e).
15a However, to the best of our
knowledge, the current studies of aminophosphination/amino-
phosphinoylation mainly focus on alkenes and alkynes. It is a
challenge to obtain vinylphosphine-substituted N-heterocycles
using conventional methods. Thus, it is highly desirable to
develop a general method for the aminophosphination of
allenes and to provide a general method for the preparation of
alkenylphosphines, which could be used as viable substrates in
subsequent organic reactions.
16 As part of our development of
an approach for the formation of C −P bonds, 17 we have, for
the ﬁrst time, disclosed a metal-free aminophosphination of
allenes toward the structurally diverse alkenylphosphines via
the bifunctionalization reaction of allenes concomitant with the
formation of the C −N and C −P bonds. This metal-free
strategy makes it easy and e ﬃcient to obtain complex
alkenylphosphine-substituted N-heterocycles, which are of
great signi ﬁcance in medical chemistry.
We initially selected N-(hexa-4,5-dien-1-yl)-4-methylbenze-
nesulfonamide 1a and diphenylphosphine oxide 2a as model
substrates and tested various Ag and Cu catalysts in di ﬀerent
solvents at di ﬀerent temperatures. Unfortunately, no phosphi-
native cyclization products were obtained. Inspired by Hirano
and Miura ’s result
15a and our previous success, 17 we carried
out the aminophosphination using 2,6-lutidine and Tf 2O. The
reaction of 1a (0.2 mmol) with 2a (0.4 mmol) in the presence
of 2,6-lutidine (0.4 mmol) and Tf 2O( 0 . 4m m o l )w a s
investigated in 1,2-dichloroethane (2 mL) for 2 h at room
temperature. To our delight, the phosphinative cyclization
product 3a was obtained in 86% yield ( Scheme 2 ).
Encouraged by this preliminary result, the scope of the
substrates was studied. The results are summarized in Scheme
3. First, an investigation into a series of N-protecting groups
showed that sulfonyl groups ( 1a−c) provided the correspond-
ing products in 65 −86% yields. The aminophosphinoylation
product 3a′ could be obtained (72%) when the reaction
mixture was treated with H
2O2. Moreover, di ﬀerent gem-
disubstituted substrates ( 1d−e)c o u l ds t i l la ﬀord the
corresponding products in 76 −79% yields, indicating that the
reaction was not a ﬀected signi ﬁcantly by the Thorpe −Ingold
eﬀect.
Next, 2-allenylphenylmethanamine substrates were subjected
to the study to further expand the scope of the reaction and to
get important functionalized isoindolines. The results are
summarized in Scheme 4 . 2-Allenylphenylmethanamines
bearing electron-neutral ( 4a,b) or electron-donating groups
(4c) on the aryl ring were well tolerated, providing the desired
products in 90 −93% yields, whereas electron-withdrawing
groups such as F ( 4d) and NO 2 (4e) decreased the yield. In
addition, a stereogenic center at the α-position of the nitrogen
atom was introduced ( 4f,g), and the expected products were
obtained in 85 −88% yields. Con ﬁguration of the product 1,3-

experiments. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations
indicated that the energy of the antitransition state (TS1
anti)
was lower than the syn-transition state (TS1 syn), due to the
advantageous C −H···π interactions between the ethyl group
and the two phenyl groups in TS1 anti, which is absent in TS1 syn
(see Supporting Information f o rd e t a i l s ) .F o rt h e1 , 1 -
disubstituted allene 4h, the reaction proceeded successfully,
giving the desired product in 80% yield. When the substrates
with an alkyl group at the terminal allene ( 4i−j) were
subjected to the reaction, the corresponding products ( 5i−j)
were obtained in good yields. Con ﬁgurations of the product E-
5i were established by the NOESY spectrum experiments. We
also examined the substrate with a trisubstituted allene ( 4k).
Disappointingly, only the hydroamination product ( 5k) was
obtained, which might primarily result from the increased
steric hindrance of methyl groups. Moreover, the reaction
could also proceed well by using N-(2-(buta-2,3-dien-2-
yl)benzyl)-4-methylbenzenesulfonamide ( 4l) and a ﬀord the
corresponding product ( 5l) in 90% yield.
Subsequently, several phosphine oxides 2 participated in the
aminophosphination reaction with 4a, and the results were
illustrated in Scheme 5 . Di-4-tolylphosphine oxide and
di([1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)phosphine oxide provided the desired
vinyl phosphine 6a,b in moderate to good yields. Sterically,
di(naphthyl)phosphine oxide furnished the desired product
(6c,d) in a good yield. We have tried other phosphine sources,
such as HP(O)Ph(OEt), dibenzo[ c,e][1,2]oxaphosphinine 6-
oxide. However, only trace aminophosphination product was
detected.
Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicated that
the aminophosphination of sulfonamidoallene undergoes
bifunctionalization of allenes to form the C −N and C −P
bond (see Supporting Information for details).
On the basis of literature
15a and DFT calculated results, a
tentative mechanism is proposed and shown in Scheme 6. The
electrophilic phosphorus species A was generated from 2a and
Tf2O, which was coordinated to allene 1a, giving the allene-
phosphine complex B. Nucleophilic attack on the allene-
phosphine complex B, along with the C −P bond formation,
could a ﬀord intermediate C, which rapidly converted to the
corresponding alkenylphosphine intermediate D. Deprotona-
tion of intermediate D in the presence of 2,6-lutidine would
lead to the formation of the vinylphosphine-substituted
pyrrolidine product 3a.
In summary, we have successfully developed the ﬁrst
eﬃcient, metal-free intramolecular aminophosphination of
various allenes with diarylphosphine oxides, a ﬀording a rapid
strategy for a structurally diverse array of alkenylphosphine-
substituted N-heterocycle bifunctionalization reactions of
allenes concomitant with the formation of the C −N and C −
P bonds under mild conditions. Importantly, the atom
economy and operational simplicity related to this method
suggest its great potential for broad applications in the
construction of valuable alkenylphosphine-substituted N-
heterocycle frameworks in medical chemistry. Moreover,
DFT calculations suggest that the sulfonamidoallene under-
goes a bifunctionalization reaction along with the formation of
the C −Na n dC −P bonds with the in situ generated
electrophilic phosphination reagent.
■ EXPERIMENTAL SECTION
Unless otherwise noted, all reagents were purchased from commercial
suppliers and used without further puri ﬁcation. Analytical thin-layer
chromatography (TLC) was performed on silica gel GF 254. Visual-
ization was accomplished by irradiation with UV light at 254 nm or
KMnO4 stain solution. Column chromatography was performed on
silica gel (200 −300 mesh). 1H NMR spectra were recorded on a
Bruker DRX-400 spectrometer (400 MHz). Chemical shifts were
reported in parts per million (ppm) referenced to 0.0 ppm for
tetramethylsilane. Data are reported as follows: chemical shift,
multiplicity (s = singlet, d = doublet, t = triplet, q = quartet, m =
multiplet, br = broad), coupling constants (Hz), and integration.
13C{1H} NMR spectra were recorded on a Bruker DRX-400
spectrometer (100 MHz) and were fully decoupled by broadband
proton decoupling. Chemical shifts were reported in parts per million
(ppm) referenced to 77.16 ppm for CDCl 3. 31P NMR spectra were
recorded on a Bruker DRX-400 spectrometer (162 MHz). High-
resolution mass spectra (HRMS) were recorded on a Waters LCT
PremierxeTM (USA).
The allene substrates were prepared according to the general
procedure of our previous work.
